segmentCorrections.why: Drivable two-way link from the foot of Panoramic Way to Prospect St / Canyon Rd, Panoramic Hill's single exit (SB 99, p. 4). OSM: Bancroft Way, tertiary, 2 lanes, no access restriction; City Street_Centerline Seg-00193: 30 ft, 2 lanes, two-way. The County record codes it no vehicle travel and names it after the Bancroft Steps stairway, which runs from Warring St to Prospect St and is a separate feature.

geom.source: Berkeley: Alameda County Street Centerlines export (data.acgov.org), downloaded 2026-10-20; segment data revised 2015-09-26. Outside Berkeley (src.osmWay): OpenStreetMap drivable ways (Overpass API, 2026-11-01; © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL), joined to the County network at the city line.
geom.note: Projected to UTM 10N, simplified to 0.75 m. OSM ends are moved onto the nearest County node (up to 60 m) where the two networks meet.

name.source: County STREET field; outside Berkeley the OSM name, upper-cased with the County's suffix abbreviations (I-80 and CA-24 carriageways named by direction as in the County file)

cls.source: County CLASS field. Outside Berkeley mapped from OSM highway (model rule): motorway = Interstate; motorway_link, trunk_link = Ramp; trunk, primary, secondary = Principal Arterial; tertiary = Major Collector; residential, unclassified, living_street = Local

osm.source: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL (openstreetmap.org/copyright). Streets outside Berkeley, barriers and traffic circles.

exitNodes.source: Nodes where an OSM street was cut 15 m inside the DEM extent (UTM 10N x 558896-569512, y 4188272-4196124). Traffic that reaches one has left the modeled area.

fireZoneSrc.source: Outside Berkeley the City fire zones do not apply; OSM streets whose midpoint is at 90 m elevation or higher (DEM) get fireZone 2, so the hill rules for lanes, speed and parking apply (proxy:elevation>=90m). Same threshold fire.js uses for hill residential land outside the city.

trav.source: County TRVLWAY: B both ways, FT one-way in the digitized direction, TF against it, NT no vehicle travel. FT/TF meaning checked against the right-hand rule on 100 divided-street pairs (97 agree).

mode.source: path = SFEATYP PA/WK or names with STEPS/PATH/WALK; restricted = TRVLWAY NT; else vehicle

correction.source: County record corrected by data/assumptions.json network.segmentCorrections (travSrc says so): correction.county holds the County values replaced, correction.osmWay the OpenStreetMap way that, with the City layers and reports named in the note, shows the County coding is wrong. meta.segmentCorrections lists every correction with its reason. SOURCE_NOTES K1-K6.

z.source: Elevation at segment ends, bilinear from data/terrain/dem.i16 (USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar DEM, 4 m overview)

grade.source: Net grade % along digitized direction from DEM endpoint elevations

gradeMax.source: 90th percentile of ~25 m window grades along the centerline, DEM sampled every 4 m. Can be wrong where the road sits on a cut, fill, bridge or retaining wall.

gradeReliable.source: false for Interstate and Ramp (the bare-earth DEM is the ground under the structure) and where the steep grade exceeds 35% (a DEM artefact: cut, fill or retaining wall)

fireZone.source: City of Berkeley FireZones_WFL1 PLN_HILL_Z at segment midpoint

evacZone.source: Genasys zone at segment midpoint, shown as e.g. BER-006 (the City layer's zonenum field is not unique across cities). Berkeley and LBNL zones from the City of Berkeley GenasysZonesBerkeley layer, except where that layer clips a zone at the city line (BER-013, BER-069, BER-074, BER-075, LBL-004, LBL-005 and others; layers.json evacZones outlineSrc says which); those outlines, LBL-006 and every other zone come from the Genasys Protect WFS (2026-11-01).

lanes.source: [forward, backward] lanes. lanesSrc says where: city:PAV_LANES = City pavement-management lanes (total); osm:lanes = OSM lanes tag (total for two-way streets, per direction for one-way); assumption:hillsLocal = Eric, 2026-10-31: hill streets are one lane each way (applied in Oakland and Kensington hills too); assumption:byClass = data/assumptions.json (one-way OSM streets: 1 lane for Local and ramps, half the class total otherwise)

widthM.source: widthSrc says where. city: City of Berkeley Street_Centerline PAV_WIDTH_RD (pavement-management width, feet) or Narrow_Roads PAV_WIDTH_, matched to County segments by name and distance (<= 12 m). osm:width = OSM width tag. assumption:berkeleyMedian(...) = median City width of Berkeley streets of the same class in the hills or flats (one-way streets: 60% of it, at least 3.5 m per lane), used for Oakland, Albany, Emeryville and Kensington streets with no width tag.

parking.source: data/assumptions.json parking.hills / parking.flats. Hills default per Eric, 2026-10-31: parking on both sides. Not yet checked against posted no-parking signs.

clearWidthM.source: City Narrow_Roads Width_w_Parking where present; else widthM minus parked-car width per parked side (assumption)

effLanes.source: Moving lanes that fit in clearWidthM: 2 if >= 2 x access.movingLaneM, 1 if >= one lane, else 0. With one effective lane, opposing vehicles must wait for each other.

belowFireCodeWidth.source: clearWidthM below access.fireCodeClearM (20 ft unobstructed width, California Fire Code 503.2.1 for new fire apparatus access roads; context only, existing streets are not required to meet it)

engineBlocked.source: clearWidthM below access.engineClearM: a fire engine cannot get through without parked cars being moved

barrier.source: Diverters and gates from the City of Berkeley list of record, layer "Existing Traffic Calming Devices" (Berkeley_Fire_Apparatus_Route_Map_WFL1, layer 1, edited 2025-10-28; cityId = its OBJECTID); bollards, gates and blocks elsewhere from OpenStreetMap barrier nodes on a street of the same name (osm = node id). How each device channels cars is read from the OpenStreetMap street geometry around it (Overpass API, 2026-11-01; © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL): action says what the network does. closure and node split: a short connector edge (or, beyond a gate on a dead-end street, the rest of that street) closed to residents' cars; engines pass after access.barrierDelayS where OSM tags the crossing emergency=yes or it is a gate. one-way: a 15 m one-way piece, open to all. Banned turns inside an open junction are not modeled. meta.barrierSites lists every device and what was done with it.

speedMps.source: data/assumptions.json capacity.speedMph by road class, capped by City SPEED where known, or by the OSM maxspeed tag outside Berkeley (outside the hills)

capPerLaneVph.source: AB 747 report capacity rules (HCM 2022): two-lane roads 45 pc/h per mph up to 1,700; multilane 1,900 per lane; freeway 2,250 per lane (capRule says which). Speed input is an assumption; steep segments reduced by a model rule.
